record.original_question: Do there exist polytopes P and Q such that the amalgamation class hP, Qi is nonempty and P has at least two non-isomorphic vertex-figures?

evidence.quote: Problem 15. Are there polytopes P and Q such that hP, Qi is nonempty and P has at least two non-isomorphic vertex-figures?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An abstract polytope of rank n is a partially ordered set of "faces", graded by ranks −1, 0, 1, …, n, satisfying the standard diamond and connectedness axioms of abstract polytope theory. Faces of rank 0 are called vertices and faces of rank n−1 are called facets. For a face F of an abstract polytope R, the section F/G between G < F is the subposet of faces H with G < H < F; in particular, for a vertex v of R, the vertex-figure of R at v is the section R/v, which is itself an abstract polytope of rank n−1. Two vertex-figures of R need not be isomorphic when R is not vertex-transitive.

For abstract polytopes P and Q of rank n, define the amalgamation class
   ⟨P, Q⟩ = { abstract polytopes R of rank n+1 : every facet of R is isomorphic to P, and every vertex-figure of R is isomorphic to Q }.

Question: Do there exist abstract polytopes P and Q (of the same rank) such that the amalgamation class ⟨P, Q⟩ is nonempty and such that P itself has at least two non-isomorphic vertex-figures?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears as one of 35 open problems posed by Cunningham and Pellicer (2016/2018) on k-orbit abstract polytopes. A web search did not turn up a published resolution; the question concerns the existence of an amalgamation of two polytopes when the facet polytope has non-isomorphic vertex-figures, and no source confirming or refuting such existence was located.

status_evidence.snippet: We present 35 open problems on combinatorial, geometric and algebraic aspects of k-orbit abstract polytopes.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is listed among the open problems on k-orbit polytopes; no resolution found in subsequent literature search.
